about.title: About
about.node.chair.body: I trained as an electrical engineer at the Universidad de Camagüey (BSc summa cum laude, 2008; MSc in industrial electrical systems, 2009) and I have been teaching there since the year I graduated — control engineering, industrial automation and PLCs, electric drives, and two electives I wrote myself, FPGA design and Arduino. I am a Profesor Titular, the highest academic rank in Cuban higher education.
about.node.radar.body: Weather radar came next. From 2012 to 2014 I wrote software at the Camagüey Meteorological Centre: the parser for the raw radar data, the Level III processing and database loading, the ingest into ORPG, the first web viewer. That software still runs the Cuban radar network today.
about.node.doctorate.label: Doctorate
about.node.doctorate.body: The doctorate ran in parallel. Invited to INAOE in late 2013 for my FPGA experience, I spent four years on reduct computation — an NP-hard combinatorial problem — and attacked it from both ends at once: two new algorithms, GCreduct and MinReduct, and hardware architectures to accelerate them. One investigation, defended twice: UCLV in Cuba (2019) and BUAP in Mexico (2022).
about.node.nitza.body: Since 2022 I have led software teams for clients in the United States.
about.node.ladetec.body: Since 2023 I have been a founder of LADETEC, with the radar specialists I worked beside at the meteorological centre. The thread has not changed: the algorithm and the machine it runs on, designed together.

system.title: LAMULA — the radar chain, rebuilt
system.lede: A commercial weather radar does not run without its vendor's software, and with that software you depend on someone else's licences and spare parts. LAMULA rebuilds the whole chain — from the RF front end to the viewer in the browser — while the data it puts out stays in the standard formats the rest of the field already reads. It is my own work, stage by stage, and the project on this site I would start with.
system.auto: The chain is advancing on its own — select a stage to take control.
system.status.title: Status and provenance
system.status.body:
LAMULA is open source and, today, a proof of concept — not a system in operation. What makes the chain above credible is not this repository but what it descends from: Vesta, the processing suite we built at the Cuban meteorological service between 2012 and 2014, which has been running that country's radar network ever since — a Gematronik radar among them.

Credit where it is due. The chain is my work, written largely with AI assistance, on top of a body of work that belongs to the team: parts of it start from Vesta code that was not all mine, and the only way this stops being a proof of concept and becomes a product is the experience of that whole team, not mine alone.
system.stage.rf.name: Antenna & RF front end
system.stage.rf.body: Pedestal, transmitter and receiver front end. The physical layer: this is where the returned power actually exists, and everything downstream is a question of not losing it.
system.stage.drx.name: DRX — digital receiver
system.stage.drx.body: Digital receiver on FPGA (Xilinx Vivado / Vitis / PetaLinux). Digitises and conditions the return at the earliest possible point. Hard real-time lives here, not further up the stack.
system.stage.dsp.name: DSP — moment estimation
system.stage.dsp.body: Estimation of the Doppler power spectrum moments of the weather radar signal — reflectivity Z, mean radial velocity V and spectrum width W. Filtering and removal of ground clutter. The moments reach the control processor over a 1 GbE link.
system.stage.rcp.name: RCP — control processor & operator MMI
system.stage.rcp.body: Runs the radar control logic, power-up and positioning routines, and organises and formats the moment files it receives. Archives the volume observation as NEXRAD Level-II and feeds ORPG in real time by fully emulating the WSR-88D RDA standard (ICD 2620002) — emulating the interface rather than licensing the vendor's. A swappable hardware abstraction layer exposes one interface with two adapters: the real plant over Modbus TCP / Profibus, and a faithful simulator, so control logic can be developed without the radar.
system.stage.orpg.name: ORPG — product generation
system.stage.orpg.body: The RCP deliberately generates no meteorological products. It archives base observations and acts as the RDA; product generation is delegated to ORPG, which emits Level III. Clean separation of responsibilities, and standard interfaces at the boundary.
system.stage.pipeline.name: Level III ingest pipeline
system.stage.pipeline.body: Headless Python service: decodes Level III PDB / Symbology / Tabular blocks, regrids to an azimuthal-equidistant projection, and writes Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFFs plus catalogue metadata and extracted phenomena.
system.stage.viewer.name: WebViewer
system.stage.viewer.body: Product viewer rendering the COGs directly in the browser with OpenLayers WebGL. Read-only by design: it neither generates nor persists data — the pipeline owns the data contract.

ask.faq.chain.q: What exactly did he build in the radar chain?
ask.faq.chain.a: Seven stages, from the FPGA digital receiver to the WebGL product viewer, with the control processor presenting itself to ORPG as a WSR-88D RDA rather than licensing the vendor's.
ask.faq.status.a: No. It is open source and a proof of concept. What runs is Vesta, the suite the team built at the Cuban meteorological service, which has driven that network since 2014.
ask.faq.phd.a: Fast algorithms for reduct computation — an NP-hard combinatorial problem — attacked from both ends at once: two new algorithms, GCreduct and MinReduct, and hardware architectures to accelerate them.
ask.faq.team.a: Since 2022, at Nitza Develop, for clients in the United States: the back-office platform, a VoIP product with web, Android and iOS clients, and a custom ERP that began as a solo job.
ask.faq.teaching.a: Control engineering, industrial automation and PLCs, electric drives, sequential system design on FPGA with VHDL, and Arduino for electrical engineers.
